title: Judea under Rome
lead: Judea, the Jewish homeland, as a Roman possession: ruled by governors in the Gospels and Acts, the scene of the revolt of AD 66 to 70, and a place where armies swore oaths to emperors in 69.

sections.b: Tacitus puts Judea in his survey of the East: Vespasian runs the war there with three legions, Nero having chosen him (1:10), and in 69 the army of Judea swore Otho's oath (1:76). Josephus says Nero chose Vespasian to punish the Jews and to stop the trouble spreading (Jewish War 3.1.2).
sections.refs: Histories of Tacitus 1:10; Histories of Tacitus 1:76; Histories of Tacitus 5:1-13

sections.b: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea (Matthew 2:1), and Pontius Pilate governed Judea in Tiberius's fifteenth year (Luke 3:1). Jesus said those in Judea must run for the hills when Jerusalem was encircled (Luke 21:21).
